assumptions: Epifany's network model, with the posterior error probabilities given as input.
The alpha, beta and gamma parameters chosen, or the grid search's.
limits: A posterior under this model: it moves with the parameters, which the answer reports.
Garbage posterior error probabilities in, garbage posteriors out.
bio.jane/contract.question: What is the posterior probability that each protein, group and match is present?

description: Bayesian protein inference, Epifany (validated against OpenMS BayesianProteinInferenceAlgorithm on PXD000001): the posterior probability that each protein, each indistinguishable group and each peptide-spectrum match is present, from the matches' posterior error probabilities under a network in which present proteins emit their peptides. Shared peptides are weighed between their proteins instead of being counted for each.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

alpha.description: peptide emission probability α: the chance a present protein yields a given one of its peptides.

appendReversedDecoys.description: add the reversed sequence of every database protein as a decoy (accession decoyPrefix + accession), for a database searched with reversed decoys that holds only targets.

beta.description: spurious emission probability β: the chance a peptide is reported with none of its proteins present.

database.description: the protein database searched, as FASTA; the accession is the header up to the first space.

decoyPrefix.description: accession prefix marking a decoy protein, for the grid search.

gamma.description: protein prior γ: the chance a protein is present before any evidence.

gridSearch.description: choose α, β and γ instead: run OpenMS's grid (α 0.1–0.8 × β 0.01–0.4 × γ 0.2–0.7) and keep the combination whose protein posteriors best agree with target-decoy FDR and separate targets from decoys; needs decoy proteins.

ilEquivalent.description: treat isoleucine and leucine (and a database J) as the same residue when mapping peptides.

maxAmbiguousResidues.description: how many ambiguous database residues (B, J, Z, X) one peptide match may resolve.

peptidePrior.description: peptide prior π, dividing each match's probability back out of its evidence.

psmCutoff.description: drop matches whose probability (1 − PEP) is below this.

psms.description: the matches as a table with a header row naming spectrum, peptide, charge and a posterior error probability column (tab- or comma-separated); peptides are ProForma.

scoreColumn.description: the column holding each match's posterior error probability (PEP, 0 to 1).

name: bayesian_protein_inference

grid.description: with the grid search: every α, β, γ tried, with its FDR-curve difference, ROC-100 and objective (skipped when improbable)

groups.description: indistinguishable protein groups, most probable first: probability that at least one member is present, and accessions

proteins.description: one row per protein: accession, posterior probability, matches counted, sequence coverage (%)

psmPosteriors.description: the matches inference used (the best per peptide): spectrum, peptide, prior (1 − PEP) and posterior
